operations.name: Samuel Green

expected.charges: Knowingly possessing a copy of Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin as prohibited abolitionist literature, under Maryland's 1841 statute making such possession by a free Black person a felony carrying ten to twenty years. Arraigned April 17, 1857.
expected.sentence:
Ten years, THE STATUTORY MINIMUM under Maryland's 1841 law, which required ten to twenty years for a free Black person knowingly possessing prohibited abolitionist publications. Arraigned April 17, 1857; convicted May 14, 1857; received at the Maryland Penitentiary in Baltimore on May 18, 1857 as prisoner number 5146, recorded as about fifty-five. Governor Augustus W. Bradford granted a conditional pardon on March 26, 1862 requiring him to leave Maryland within sixty days, and he was released on April 21, 1862 -- four years, eleven months and three days served against a projected expiry of May 14, 1867.

THE COUNTER RUNS FROM THE PENITENTIARY ADMISSION, not from the April 4 arrest. He was jailed after the arrest, but the Dorchester County jail ledger has not been consulted and continuity of that detention is not established. Counting from April 4 would publish about five years and seventeen days as though documented; counting from May 18 publishes the 1,799 days that are.

operations.source: Maryland State Archives biographical study: https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/013700/013785/html/13785bio.html . Names trial judge and state attorney. Existing May 18, 1857 admission and April 21, 1862 release already populated; preserved. Applied only to Uncle Toms Cabin conviction row.
